title: Check the time axis and units of a test CSV first
summary: Check units, missing values, finite numbers, and duplicate or reversed timestamps in synthetic demonstration data, then save the check results and a chart.
audience: Engineers and beginners reading a vehicle test CSV with Python for the first time
prerequisites: Have Python 3.12 and a terminal ready. Check the version with python --version.
Extract the entire downloaded ZIP and open a terminal in the folder containing example.py.
Start with the included practice data, then compare the results with the original files.
The included synthetic_test.csv is synthetic demonstration data. It uses s for time and km/h for speed.

sections.heading: Four things to check before charting

blocks.text: First check the file structure, numbers, units, and time order of the synthetic demonstration data. Being able to read the values does not tell you that the units are right or the times are correct. This example checks that s and km/h are stated in every input row and that time increases in the original row order.

blocks.title: Please check
blocks.text: The input, output, and chart are all synthetic demonstration data. They do not judge the performance, regulatory compliance, or safety of a real vehicle.

Do not attach unit strings to numeric cells. Record units in a separate column. time cannot be negative, and at least two samples are required. This code does not define a physically normal range for speed.

sections.heading: Prepare the files and run the example

items: Extract the ZIP and check that the input file listed in README.txt is in the same folder as example.py. Do not run the example from inside the ZIP archive.
Run the commands below one line at a time in the folder containing example.py. On Windows, if python is unavailable but py is available, replace python in each command with py -3.12.
After the completion message appears, open the new outputs folder. If outputs already exists, first rename it to keep the previous results, then run the example again.

blocks.text: Installation requires an internet connection. BASE in the code sets the input and output paths relative to example.py, not the current terminal folder.

While reading each row of the CSV, it checks for missing values and units. math.isfinite rejects NaN and infinity. If the current time is less than or equal to the previous time, it stops, so it does not hide problems by sorting or arbitrarily delete duplicate samples. outputs is created only after the input check is finished.

outputs/data_check.json records the units, number of samples, time range, and the minimum and maximum sampling interval. outputs/synthetic_speed.png is a chart of the same synthetic demonstration data.

headers: Results for the included synthetic demonstration data

blocks.text: Because of floating-point representation, the sampling interval in the JSON may appear as 0.19999999999999996. It is not a number that claims any additional precision of the input values or measurement resolution.

items: Check that sample_count in the normal result is 6 and time_unit is s.
In a freshly extracted practice folder, change the time of the third data row to equal the previous value, 0.2. When run, it should stop with the message duplicate or decreasing time.
In another fresh copy, change one speed_unit to m/s. Check that the expected units message appears and outputs is not created.
Keep the original input file, and run error experiments only on copies.

sections.heading: What to look at when the check stops

headers: What to check in the original
rows: Check that the export settings match the units in each row. The code does not convert automatically.
Check whether the time order changed during a restart, duplicate samples, or file merging.
Check the original for missing samples or calculation errors.
Keep the label marking it as synthetic demonstration data for this tutorial only.
Check the number of commas, blank cells, and column names.

sections.heading: What still needs checking after the check passes

items: It does not enforce a rule that the time interval must be constant. If min_interval_s and max_interval_s differ, check the original's sampling period separately.
It does not perform filtering, interpolation, unit conversion, sensor calibration, time synchronization, or noise judgments.
It checks only the notation in the unit columns. It cannot confirm that the actual values were measured in that unit or that the sensor is on the right channel.
This is file-handling practice limited to the included data. Do not interpret it as a validation tool that can be used for real vehicle test procedures or safety judgments.

verification.env: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), CPython 3.12.14 (64-bit). openpyxl 3.1.5, Matplotlib 3.10.8. The libraries used by each example are pinned in requirements.txt.
items: Checked 6 samples of synthetic demonstration data, the time range, units, and intervals
Checked errors for unit mismatch, duplicate or reversed times, NaN, and missing values
Checked that the original hash is unchanged, existing results are refused, and the PNG is created
limits: Only synthetic demonstration data was checked. Real measurement data and vehicle safety were not evaluated.
